original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Exact cost of invertible two-role right-vector targets over finite products of associative local K-algebras: radical invariance of the two-factor set, cost_R(M)=max(delta_R(M),cost_(R/J)(Mbar))<=3, and the sharp field-size component threshold. Literal exhaustive finite controls over (F2[e]/e^2)^k for k=1,2,3.
scope_change_reason: Takes Open next question 1 of ToikY #4334 rather than a new native register construction. The result separates radical effects from common residue charts; this is a formal-alphabet side result.
bottleneck_link: Side result for a formal two-role alphabet; it settles the effect of local radicals on exact factor counts. Native conversion, physical caller and complete supplier costs remain unknown, and no kappa changes.
stop_rule: Stop after the radical-reduction proof and first complete binary dual-number product controls; package the result without a larger construction or search campaign.
evidence: PROOF.md gives the scoped proof. verify.py enumerates literal words with zero, one and two paid factors and an explicit three-factor upper witness. All 894048 invertible targets over one, two and three binary dual-number factors satisfy the maximum formula; exactly 49152 of the three-component targets cost three. No predecessor verifier is imported or replayed.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does radical invariance of the two-factor set extend from products of local algebras to all semilocal K-algebras?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Matrix blocks in the semisimple quotient allow nontrivial ranks and fall outside the local division-residue proof.
open_questions.first_step: Specify the two-factor unit-pivot criterion and an explicit three-factor construction when R/J has one M2(K) block; separate radical lifting from the block obstruction.
open_questions.blocked_by: The present proof uses the component ideal of non-units; matrix algebras do not satisfy that hypothesis.

open_questions.question: Which singular targets over local products have finite cost, and is three always sufficient for the reachable ones?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Invertibility is used both in the unit-pivot reduction and in choosing the three-factor word; singular radical targets can be unreachable.
open_questions.first_step: Characterise the three-factor image over F2[x,y]/(x,y)^2 before attempting a general theorem.
open_questions.blocked_by: No unit-pivot reduction or general reachability theorem for singular targets is proved here.
